To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) people have well-developed schemata regarding the personality characteristics of people in a number of occupations; (2) people's schemata for occupations are not random but rather are organized into two broad categories of achievement and helping; (3) people's schematas for occupations are organized in the same way regardless of their own personality; and (4) people's schemats for occupations are organized similarly across the sexes.

the predominant dimension that differentiates the perceived personalities of people in various occupations is achievement orientation versus helping or nurturing orientation, and that the second most important dimension is the extent to which people are perceived as being concerned with self versus concerned with others.

the perceived personality of people in different occupations is organized in a multidimensional fashion and that the major dimensions of this organization reflect achievement orientation vs. helping orientation and introversion vs. extraversion.

the nature of stereotyped occupational role information.
the nature of stereotypic information about occupations and the personality characteristics associated with them.

the personality characteristics associated with occupations are not as stereotyped as has been assumed in the past.
